page: Microsoft Azure E4s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine configured with 4 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8171M processor running at 2.6 GHz, this instance utilizes Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization on an x86_64 architecture. The underlying CPU features 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, a 35 MB L3 cache, and support for AVX and AVX512F instruction sets. Local storage is limited to a 66 GB temporary disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates that the E4s_v3 exhibits limited processing and memory throughput capabilities. In stress-ng CPU tests, both single-core and multi-core performance fall into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, including read-only operations for both small and large blocks, register in the bottom 10%, with large block write speeds remaining in the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations and Redis SET performance are constrained, with Redis operations scoring in the bottom 10% at 2.53 million operations per second.

From a resource density perspective, the E4s_v3 provides a high memory allocation relative to its compute footprint, making it a candidate for memory-bound workloads that do not require high CPU throughput. However, the tradeoff is a lower performance-per-resource profile in compute-heavy tasks, as evidenced by weak scores in software compilation, compression, and LLM inference. This server is suited for small-scale databases, caching layers, or memory-intensive enterprise applications with moderate processing demands.
description: Microsoft Azure E4s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8171M processor at 2.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, it includes 2 physical cores, a 35 MB L3 cache, and a 66 GB local storage disk. Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers, with stress-ng CPU and memory bandwidth tests scoring in the bottom 10% to 25%. The high 8.0 GB memory-per-vCPU ratio offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy, compute-light workloads, though it faces performance tradeoffs in processing-intensive tasks. It is suited for small database operations, caching, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
